The distinction between Type I and Type II SOC 2 assessments reflects a duality in temporal modeling: Type I is a static snapshot (Bayesian prior), while Type II is a dynamic trajectory (temporal kernel). The former evaluates control design at a point in time, whereas the latter evaluates operational consistency over a duration. This duality implies a bifurcation in compliance modeling: one rooted in static design verification and another in stochastic process monitoring. Failure modes include misalignment between design and operation, or insufficient temporal coverage of evidence. The temporal kernel of Type II introduces a continuity constraint on evidence, requiring sustained observability rather than discrete validation.
